transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello. Well, I suppose what finally made me come in is this issue I'm having when I drive. The moment my car reaches one of those long bridges heading toward Miami, my chest just tightens right up. My hands clamp down on the steering wheel, and I get this... this sudden certainty that I have to get off the bridge immediately. Even though there’s obviously nowhere to go.
Do you experience these feelings only when you are on bridges, or do they happen in other situations as well?

No, it's really just the bridges. I don't have this problem anywhere else. Just... when I'm driving over the water on those long spans. Everywhere else, whether I'm driving around town or just going about my day, I'm perfectly fine. It's only the bridges.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear when crossing bridges?

It's been about 11 months now. That's when my daughter’s heart condition started, and she needed to start seeing a specialist down in Miami on a regular basis. I've had to drive her to those appointments, and... well, that's when all this started happening.
